normalization.title: When Every AI Website Looks Good, What Makes One Actually Work?

source.title: I Studied 10,000 AI Websites… Here’s what I learned
source.creator: Nate Herk | AI Automation

normalization.overview: Five practical design heuristics distinguish functional interfaces from polished but generic AI-generated pages.
normalization.whyItMatters: Marketing conversion heuristics cannot be copied without qualification into operational consoles; evidence, authority and task completion matter.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Adopt intent-first copy, semantic emphasis, functional depth, purposeful motion and interactive proof; test comprehension and task success.
normalization.falsification: Apply the five heuristics to one existing screen each in Mission Control, Hyperion Studio, SharePlane and Readers; compare comprehension, task completion, errors, accessibility and time to useful information.
normalization.freshness: November 9, 2026 source, verified private ReasonPack and local Whisper timestamped transcript; performance figures remain unverified.

claims.proposition: The presenter recommends aligning the first screen with the visitor’s intent.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: A useful design constraint, not a controlled outcome.

claims.proposition: A trucking job-page redesign reportedly improved conversion 79.3%.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: No independently inspected experimental denominator or study design.

claims.proposition: A City Click headline change reportedly increased pricing-page clickthroughs 90%.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: Reported example, not an independently replicated controlled result.

claims.proposition: A Campaign Monitor wording change reportedly increased signups 31.4%.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: Reported example, not an independently replicated controlled result.

claims.proposition: Accent color should preserve visual priority; the 60/30/10 ratio is a heuristic.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: Operational state requires multiple semantic signals and non-color cues.

claims.proposition: Spatial layers can convey hierarchy rather than decorate.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: Overlap must retain mobile and accessibility function.

claims.proposition: Animation should demonstrate, guide or explain state, with reduced-motion access.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: A single-motion maximum is a contextual marketing heuristic, not an operations law.

claims.proposition: Useful interactive output can demonstrate value before commitment.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: Utility and effort must be measured; this is not evidence every quiz improves conversion.

claims.proposition: An orthodontic calculator reportedly converted approximately 45%, according to vendor Outgrow.
claims.assessment: Source-attributed and interpreted within the locked GhostMesh analysis.
claims.limits: 45% is a conversion rate, not a lift. Denominator and selection effects unverified.
